subject: Urban Planning
title: Infrastructure Equity: Who Gets Served?
description: A quick, practical guide to Infrastructure Equity: Who Gets Served?.

hook.text: Flint, Michigan went two years drinking lead-poisoned water. Wealthy suburbs nearby had clean water the entire time.

buildup.text: Infrastructure investment follows wealth. Rich areas get new pipes, roads, and broadband. Poor areas get deferred maintenance.

discovery.text: The EPA found that communities of color face 1.3 times higher exposure to polluted water sources than white communities.

twist.text: Federal infrastructure funding often requires local matching funds. Poor cities can't match, so they get less federal money too.

climax.text: Justice40 directs 40% of federal infrastructure spending to disadvantaged communities. It's the first equity-centered policy.

punchline.text: Clean water for the rich. Lead pipes for the poor. Same country.

quiz.question: What does the Justice40 initiative require?
options: All infrastructure projects must be completed within 40 months
40% of federal infrastructure spending goes to disadvantaged communities
Cities must allocate 40% of their budget to infrastructure repair
